correctness.rationale: Direct bit-mask enumeration checks all 8192 potential point sets, constructs all thirteen 4-point lines, all 247 minimal transversals and the complete 3–6 point trace spectra. A separate affine-coordinate implementation independently obtains the same spectra and a Littlestone rank six. A complete 63-internal-query depth-six tree with 64 consistent distinct leaves is replayed, and the maximum blocker size six excludes a depth-seven all-positive path. The Fano control class is enumerated and dimension additivity on disjoint unions is proved.

claim_vs_prior_implication.reasoning: We claim neither first discovery of projective-plane minimal blockers nor the number of geometric types. The claimed advance is that their point-membership concept class has a sharp 5-versus-6 separation, precisely described shattered supports and an unbounded extension to linear four-uniform four-regular point-transitive hypergraphs. The accessible 2022 classification does determine the underlying objects and could in principle support derivation of some statistics, so historical-priority risk is real. Its accessible abstract does not directly establish these learning invariants, and the separately motivated geometric shattered-support statement and uniform amplification are not explicit consequences stated in the compared sources.

value.rationale: The exact 702 shattered 5-supports and their two-triangle completion property yield an interpretable structural classification, not a bare count. The depth-six adaptive tree shows a strict 5-vs-6 static/online separation for a canonical finite incidence geometry. Disjoint-union additivity gives an unbounded separation within point-transitive, linear, 4-uniform, 4-regular hypergraphs (necessarily disconnected in this construction). No general arbitrary-order projective-plane claim is made.
